title: Seeded world
plain: The game map is built from a single number called the seed. Give it the same seed and you get exactly the same map, every time.
why: A route can only be trusted and replayed if the map never changes between runs.
done_when: Two worlds from the same seed are identical byte for byte, and every seed gives a playable map.

title: Counting the map's shape
plain: Topology just means counting the shape of the map: how many separate islands of open ground there are (b0) and how many rings that walk around a hole (b1).
why: Knowing the shape first tells the planner what is reachable before it wastes time searching.
done_when: The fast counts match a slow trusted count on 100 different seeds.

title: Surgery: dig and place
plain: When the runner digs or places one block, the island and ring counts are fixed on the spot instead of counting the whole map again.
why: A speedrun digs constantly, so each dig must be cheap to understand.
done_when: After every dig or place, the quick counts equal a full recount.

title: Routing and the any% run
plain: The planner finds the fastest way to win, using the tech tree (what you must make before what) and the shape of the map, then races a plain search.
why: This is the point of the project: a faster finish time than a simple search at the same thinking time.
done_when: On a fixed list of seeds the planner finishes in fewer game ticks than the baseline, with the same route every run.

title: The plain-English website
plain: One web page lists every goal in simple words with a live badge showing whether it is not started, failing or passing.
why: Anyone can see how far the project has got without reading code.
done_when: The page opens at http://localhost:7740 and shows every goal and its status.

title: Project skeleton
plain: Set up the empty Rust project with three small code libraries: world, topology and route.
why: Every other goal needs a known place to put its code.
done_when: All three libraries build and can call each other.

title: Top-level project file
plain: Create the main Rust project file that says every code library lives in one folder.
why: One shared project means one build folder and the computer's memory stays safe.
done_when: Cargo can read the project file without errors.

title: Three empty libraries
plain: Create the world, topology and route libraries as empty files that already know about each other.
why: Later goals then only fill in files, so they never collide.
done_when: One small test in the route library builds and runs, using all three libraries.

title: Repeatable random numbers
plain: Turn a seed and a map position into a random-looking number that is always the same for the same input.
why: Everything in the world grows from this, so repeatable here means repeatable everywhere.
done_when: The same input always gives the same number, and different inputs give different numbers.

title: Smooth noise
plain: Make noise where nearby spots get similar numbers, so the ground forms hills and caves instead of static.
why: Real-looking terrain has connected caves and islands, which is what the topology counts.
done_when: Neighbouring points differ by small amounts and all values stay between 0 and 1.

title: The map grid
plain: The map is a grid of squares, each one air, stone, water, tree, iron or the finish flag, and it can be saved as plain bytes.
why: Every other part reads this one shared map.
done_when: Saving a grid to bytes and loading it back gives the same grid.

title: Build world from seed
plain: Use the noise to decide where stone, water, caves and ores go, and build the whole map from the seed.
why: This is the world the runner will actually be raced through.
done_when: Building twice from the same seed gives the same bytes.

title: Every seed is playable
plain: Check that every seed gives a start square, trees, iron and a finish flag.
why: A map with no iron or no flag cannot be speedrun, so none may slip through.
done_when: All of 100 seeds have a start, trees, iron and a finish flag.

title: Pinned world fingerprint
plain: Save a short fingerprint of the map for seed 7, and fail if it ever changes.
why: It catches a silent change to the map that would break every saved route.
done_when: Seed 7 gives the same fingerprint as the one written down in the test.

title: Slow trusted island counter
plain: Walk the map square by square and count the separate islands of open ground.
why: A simple slow count is the answer key the fast methods are marked against.
done_when: It gets the right island count on small hand-drawn maps.

title: Fast club-joining tool
plain: Squares that touch join the same club, and the number of clubs is the number of islands.
why: It is the engine of the whole solver: it counts islands fast and keeps counting as the map changes.
done_when: It reports the right number of clubs after a list of joins.

title: Euler number
plain: Count corners, edges and filled squares to get one score that equals islands minus rings.
why: It is a cheap way to find the rings (b1), and it can be updated from a single block.
done_when: A ring-shaped map scores zero and a solid blob scores one.

title: Islands and rings together
plain: Combine the club count and the Euler number to report both islands (b0) and rings (b1).
why: One call gives the planner the full shape of the map.
done_when: A ring of open ground reports one island and one ring.

title: Check against 100 seeds
plain: Compare the fast counts with the slow trusted counts on 100 seeds.
why: Agreement on many different maps is the proof the topology is right.
done_when: All 100 seeds agree on both the island count and the ring count.

title: Reachable islands first
plain: Before planning, list the islands the player can reach, so items sealed in an unreachable pocket are ruled out.
why: Ruling out dead ends for free saves the planner its search time.
done_when: An ore sealed behind water is reported as unreachable.

title: Local score change
plain: Look only at the eight squares around a block to work out how the Euler score changes when it flips between wall and open.
why: It makes each dig cost a few steps, not a recount of the whole map.
done_when: Its answer matches a full recount for all 256 possible neighbourhoods.

title: Dig a block
plain: Dig out one block and update the island and ring counts immediately.
why: Digging joins islands and can close rings, which is how shortcuts appear.
done_when: After a dig, the counts equal a full recount.

title: Place a block
plain: Place a block on open ground and update the counts, even when it cuts an island in two.
why: The runner may need to wall things off, and the counts must stay true.
done_when: After placing a block, the counts equal a full recount.

title: Random edit stress test
plain: Dig and place hundreds of random blocks on 100 seeds, checking after every edit.
why: One lucky case proves nothing, so this tries to break the quick method everywhere.
done_when: Quick counts equal the full recount after every edit on every seed.

title: Preview a dig
plain: Say how many islands a dig would join and whether it would close a ring, without doing it.
why: The planner can compare walls and choose the best one to dig.
done_when: The preview matches what really happens when the dig is done.

title: Shortest-path finder
plain: Write the standard shortest-path method (Dijkstra) for any map of costs.
why: It is the ground truth every faster planner is measured against.
done_when: It agrees with a slow brute-force method on random cost maps.

title: Rules of time
plain: Set how many game ticks a walk, a dig or a craft takes, with a pickaxe making digging faster.
why: The fastest route depends on what each action really costs.
done_when: Digging stone takes fewer ticks with a pickaxe than by hand.

title: Tech tree chart
plain: Write what you must have before you can make the next thing, and sort it so prerequisites come first.
why: It tells the planner which items to fetch, and in what order, to reach the goal.
done_when: Every item appears after everything it needs, and a loop is reported as an error.

title: A moment in a run
plain: Describe one moment as where you stand and what you carry, and list the moves allowed, such as no iron without a stone pickaxe.
why: The route is a search through these moments, so they must follow the game's rules.
done_when: Mining iron is refused without a stone pickaxe and allowed with one.

title: The route planner
plain: Search for the fastest run, first asking the map's shape whether the goal can be reached at all.
why: It is the solver's output: the quickest known way to win.
done_when: Its time equals the plain shortest-path answer on a fixed list of seeds.

title: The rival planner
plain: A plain search that counts moves instead of time and stops when its budget runs out.
why: Beating a fair simple rival is how we know the planner is really good.
done_when: It returns a legal route that reaches the goal.

title: Race the rival
plain: Run the planner and the rival on the same seeds with the same thinking time.
why: This is the real test of the project: fewer game ticks than the rival.
done_when: The planner finishes in fewer ticks and gives the same route each time it runs.

title: Goal cards page
plain: One web page loads the goal list and shows each goal as a card with a title, a plain explanation and why it matters.
why: It turns the plan into something anyone can read.
done_when: A check script finds one card for every goal in the list.

title: Live status badges
plain: Each card gets a badge (not started, failing, passing) and the page refreshes its data every few seconds.
why: Progress shows without anyone touching the page.
done_when: A check script finds a badge on every card and the refresh in the page.

title: Serve on port 7740
plain: Start the page on this computer only, at address 127.0.0.1, port 7740.
why: This is the address the owner opens to watch the project.
done_when: Opening the address returns the page.

title: Numbers and noise
plain: Repeatable random numbers and smooth noise are made from the seed. They are the raw material the terrain is shaped from.
why: Everything in the world grows from these, so repeatable here means repeatable everywhere.
done_when: The same input gives the same number, and neighbouring spots get similar values.

title: The map and its builder
plain: The map is a grid of squares, and a builder fills it in from the seed.
why: This is the world the runner is raced through.
done_when: A grid saves and loads unchanged, and the same seed builds the same bytes.

title: Playable and pinned
plain: Every seed must give a playable world, and a fingerprint of one world is saved so it can never change by accident.
why: A map with no iron or flag cannot be speedrun, and a silent change would break saved routes.
done_when: All 100 seeds are playable and seed 7 matches its fingerprint.

title: Two island counters
plain: A slow trusted counter and a fast club-joining counter both count the islands of open ground.
why: The slow one is the answer key, the fast one is the engine of the solver.
done_when: Both count the right islands on small hand-drawn maps.

title: Euler number and rings
plain: The Euler number is combined with the island count to give islands (b0) and rings (b1) together.
why: One call gives the planner the full shape of the map.
done_when: A ring of open ground reports one island and one ring.

title: Checks and reachable islands
plain: The fast counts are checked on 100 seeds, and the islands the player can reach are listed before any planning.
why: Agreement on many maps is the proof, and ruling out dead ends saves search time.
done_when: All 100 seeds agree, and an ore sealed behind water is reported unreachable.

title: Digging
plain: Work out and apply what digging one block does to the island and ring counts.
why: Digging joins islands and can close rings, which is how shortcuts appear.
done_when: After a dig the counts equal a full recount.

title: Placing, preview, stress test
plain: Place blocks, preview a dig without doing it, and stress-test every kind of edit against a full recount.
why: The runner edits the map constantly, so every edit must keep the counts true.
done_when: Quick counts equal the full recount after every edit on every seed.

title: Rules and shortest path
plain: The rules of the run: a shortest-path finder, the time each action costs, and the tech tree.
why: The fastest route depends on what each action really costs.
done_when: Dijkstra matches brute force, a pickaxe speeds digging, and the tech tree sorts correctly.

title: Moments and planning
plain: One moment of a run is where you stand and what you carry, and the planner searches through those moments.
why: This is the solver's output: the quickest known way to win.
done_when: The planner's time equals the plain shortest-path answer.

title: The rival and the race
plain: A plain rival planner is built, then raced against ours on the same seeds with the same thinking time.
why: Beating a fair simple rival is how we know the planner is really good.
done_when: The planner finishes in fewer ticks and gives the same route each run.

title: Goal cards with badges
plain: The web page itself: a card for every goal, each with a live status badge.
why: Anyone can see how far the project has got.
done_when: Check scripts find a card and a badge for every goal.
